market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox won the 2022 Republican primary but lost the general election by 29 points, which may weaken his standing for 2026. Republican donors and party elites are likely to coalesce behind an electable alternative, while Cox's base may be loyal but smaller than 2022 due to his poor performance. The market price of 57.5% overstates his chances given the strong odds of a competitive challenger emerging.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 general election by 29 points to Wes Moore, a disastrous result for a gubernatorial candidate.
The 2022 primary featured a Trump-endorsed conservative vs. a Hogan-backed moderate; Cox won with 52%, but that was before his general election wipeout.
Maryland Republican primary voters historically nominate hard-right candidates, but there is a track record of past losers being replaced by fresh faces in subsequent primaries.
sources_consulted: Historical primary data for Maryland Republican gubernatorial primaries (Ballotpedia)
News articles on potential 2026 Republican candidates (The Baltimore Sun)
